inputs.text: [excited] Here comes the Jurassic! [happily] One hundred eighty million years ago. [chuckles] Its name comes from the Jura mountains, [playful] between France and Switzerland.
[curious] Had the continents moved?
[amazed] [pauses] Pangea starts to crack. [calm] A long rift opens in the middle, [softly] and a sea slowly settles in.
[curious] Is it hot?
[happily] Hot and humid! [playful] Huge fern forests grow everywhere, [calm] along with conifers and ginkgos.
[gasps] What's a ginkgo?
[chuckles] A tree with fan-shaped leaves. [amazed] And the wildest part: it still exists today, [softly] almost the same!
[excited] Did the dinos eat all that?
[happily] So much of it! [excited] So much food that the plant-eaters grew huge. [shouts] Diplodocus, almost as long as an Olympic pool!
[amazed] Wow…
[warmly] Brachiosaurus raised its long neck straight up, [calm] like a crane, [softly] to reach the tops of the trees.
[curious] Why were they so big?
[serious] Their long necks let them eat without moving their legs. [calm] And inside their bones, [softly] tiny air pockets, [playful] light like a bird's.
[curious] What about the carnivores?
[excited] Allosaurus hunted them. [serious] Sharp teeth, [softly] powerful claws. [calm] And Stegosaurus defended itself with its spiked tail.
[curious] Were there animals in the sky?
[playful] Archaeopteryx! [gently] Almost a bird, almost a dinosaur, [softly] with feathers and small wings.
[curious] And in the ocean?
[serious] Ophthalmosaurus hunted squid [calm] with its huge eyes. [pauses] And Liopleurodon, [amazed] a powerful thirty-foot hunter, [softly] snapped its jaws shut on anything nearby.
[hesitant] Thirty feet, [pauses] is that huge?
[chuckles] As long as a tennis court. [calm] Huge, yes, but not more.
[curious] What comes after the Jurassic?
[excited] The continents keep drifting apart, [pauses] slowly, [happily] and something brand new is about to appear on Earth…
